topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
correct answer: Last night the children could stay up until eleven.
wrong options / checks: We could stay up late on Saturdays when we were kids. | We couldn't go out on school nights. | In the end we were allowed to leave early.
explanation shown to learner: Permission on one occasion: *were allowed to*, not *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* is for permission that was always there, and *couldn't* is fine for both.
explanation in Latvian: Atļauja vienā reizē: *were allowed to*, nevis *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* ir atļaujai, kas bija vienmēr, un *couldn't* der abos gadījumos.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: Choose the correct option: After driving round for three hours, we ___ find a parking space.
wrong options / checks: could | can | have been able to
explanation shown to learner: One success on one past occasion: *were able to* (or *managed to*), not *could*: *we were able to find a parking space*.
explanation in Latvian: Viens *izdevies* mēģinājums pagātnē: *were able to* (vai *managed to*), nevis *could*: *we were able to find a parking space*.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
correct answer: The forms are able to be filled in online.
wrong options / checks: I could hear the sea from my hotel room. | We were able to finish the job on time. | She'll be able to drive next year.
explanation shown to learner: Before a passive, use *can*: *The forms can be filled in online*, not *are able to be*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms ciešamās kārtas lieto *can*: *The forms can be filled in online*, nevis *are able to be*.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
correct answer: May the figures in the report be wrong?
wrong options / checks: The results may point to a wider problem. | Could the figures be wrong? | Is she likely to accept the offer?
explanation shown to learner: We don't ask about possibility with *May…?*: *Could the figures be wrong?* or *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*
explanation in Latvian: Par iespējamību nejautā ar *May*…?: *Could the figures be wrong?* vai *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: Choose the correct option: The next bus is in an hour, so we ___ walk.
wrong options / checks: might as good | might so well | might well as
explanation shown to learner: *might / may as well* + base verb = it is the only sensible thing to do: *we might as well walk*.
explanation in Latvian: *might / may as well* + pamatforma = tas ir vienīgais saprātīgais: *we might as well walk*.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: You ___ me you were bringing five friends! I would have made more food. (might / warn)
explanation shown to learner: *You might have* + past participle: you should have done it (a reproach): *You might have warned me!*
explanation in Latvian: *You might have* + 3. forma: *tev* vajadzēja to izdarīt (pārmetums): *You might have warned me!*

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Crete. (may / lie)
correct answer: may be lying | might be lying
explanation shown to learner: A possible activity at a future moment: *may be* + *-ing*, *I may be lying on a beach*.
explanation in Latvian: Iespējama darbība nākotnes brīdī: *may be + -ing, I may be lying on a beach*.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: He didn't sound serious about leaving. He ___ . (might / joke)
correct answer: might have been joking | might have joked
explanation shown to learner: A possible activity in the past: *might have been* + *-ing*, *he might have been joking*.
explanation in Latvian: Iespējama darbība pagātnē: *might have been + -ing, he might have been joking*.

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
task: Choose the correct option: Winters here ___ very long, so bring warm clothes.
wrong options / checks: can being | are able to be | could have been
explanation shown to learner: *can* for what is sometimes or typically true: *Winters here can be very long.*
explanation in Latvian: *can* tam, kas mēdz būt vai ir raksturīgi: *Winters here can be very long.*

topic: Advanced modals: can, be able to, may, might
correct answer: She may not much experience, but she learns fast.
wrong options / checks: The flat may be small, but it's bright and quiet. | He might not be the fastest, but he never gives up. | It may well rain later, so take an umbrella.
explanation shown to learner: *may not* + base verb: *She may not have much experience, but she learns fast.*
explanation in Latvian: *may not* + pamatforma: *She may not have much experience, but she learns fast.*
